bibliographic.title: ChatGPT in medicine: an overview of its applications, advantages, limitations, future prospects, and ethical considerations
bibliographic.authors: Tirth Dave, Sai Anirudh Athaluri, Satyam Singh
bibliographic.citation_apa: Dave, T., Athaluri, S. A., & Singh, S. (2023). ChatGPT in medicine: An overview of its applications, advantages, limitations, future prospects, and ethical considerations. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 6, 1169595. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2023.1169595

methodology.technology_context: ChatGPT (GPT family language model), virtual assistants, natural language processing in medical and healthcare domains

eligibility.decision_rationale: Mini review focused on ChatGPT applications, limitations, and ethical considerations in medicine. Relevant as supporting evidence for regulated healthcare use of conversational LLMs and transparency/legal concerns, but provided text does not substantiate operational conversational governance mechanisms (guardrails, audit, oversight workflows).
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter (page 1) was supplied; full-text review needed to verify depth of governance, oversight, monitoring, and compliance content beyond ethical overview.

appraisal.notes: Peer-reviewed mini review with clear stated scope in abstract. No search strategy, inclusion criteria, or systematic synthesis method is visible in the provided excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: Abstract and introduction coherently frame ChatGPT medical applications and ethical/legal risks, but governance-operational content is thin in the supplied text and review methodology is not described.

coding.subtheme: Ethical and legal considerations of ChatGPT in healthcare
rq_alignment: ethics and transparency in LLM use

synthesis.main_claim: ChatGPT offers broad potential medical and healthcare applications, including virtual assistants for patients, but its use raises ethical and legal concerns such as copyright infringement, medico-legal complications, and the need for transparency in AI-generated content.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a peer-reviewed overview of ChatGPT applications, advantages, limitations, future prospects, and ethical considerations specifically in medicine and healthcare.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text is limited to page 1; no review methodology, governance framework, or operational controls are evidenced. Claims about detailed ethical analysis are asserted but not demonstrated in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting contextual evidence on ChatGPT in regulated healthcare and high-level ethical/legal transparency concerns; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance mechanisms without full-text confirmation.

evidence.claim: Article is a peer-reviewed mini review in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence (2023).
evidence.excerpt: TYPE Mini Review PUBLISHED 04 May 2023 DOI 10.3389/frai.2023.1169595

evidence.claim: Study focuses specifically on ChatGPT in healthcare/medicine.
evidence.excerpt: This paper presents an analysis of the advantages, limitations, ethical considerations, future prospects, and practical applications of ChatGPT and artificial intelligence (AI) in the healthcare and medical domains.

evidence.claim: ChatGPT is characterized as a specific large publicly available GPT language model.
evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT is an advanced language model that uses deep learning techniques to produce human-like responses to natural language inputs.
The development of virtual assistants to aid patients in managing their health is another important application of ChatGPT in medicine.

evidence.claim: Raises ethical and legal concerns relevant to governance discourse.
evidence.excerpt: the use of ChatGPT and other AI tools in medical writing also poses ethical and legal concerns.

evidence.claim: Mentions transparency as an ethical requirement.
evidence.excerpt: These include possible infringement of copyright laws, medico-legal complications, and the need for transparency in AI-generated content.

evidence.claim: Acknowledges limitations and ethical considerations as core outputs.
evidence.excerpt: However, these applications come with several limitations and ethical considerations which are presented in detail along with future prospects in medicine and healthcare.

evidence.claim: No systematic review methodology is evidenced in the provided text.
